title: Court-held funds can reach every worker in a small enforcement case while adequacy and durable recovery remain unknown
source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman enforcement follow-up for Atkins Freight Services truck drivers

observations.period: 2007–2009 underpayment; January 17, 2018 appeal-dismissal and payment follow-up

denominator.unit: truck drivers named in the official enforcement follow-up; no population denominator

ordered_backpay.unit: Australian dollars plus superannuation and interest

payment_instrument_and_adequacy.unit: missing independent transfer evidence, household effect, and adequacy assessment

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman appeal-dismissal release; court-held funds, release, reported worker-level receipt, and later recovery are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The follow-up reports receipt institutionally but is not an independent payment audit. Ten workers in one case cannot estimate enforcement or payment success rates; later work, household security, health, trust, recurrence, and exit are not followed.
observations.subgroup: Ten truck drivers underpaid minimum wages and entitlements by Atkins Freight Services; the company appealed after funds were paid into Court.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported receipt for every worker can coexist with delayed payment, residual loss, inadequate household recovery, and unresolved trust; formal remedy completion is not durable security.

related_sources.claim: Official Fair Work Ombudsman account of appeal dismissal, trust release, ordered back-pay, and reported driver receipts.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the committed project ledger containing the bounded official-release extraction.
reproduction_audit.access_boundary: The institutional follow-up reports receipt ranges but not payment instruments, independent worker confirmation, adequacy, later work, household recovery, trust, recurrence, health, or exit.

boundary: This record closes a reported payment-receipt endpoint for ten workers after court enforcement and appeal. It does not establish independent receipt verification, adequacy, durable recovery, prevalence, or general enforcement performance.
